author: blu
body: Do NOT reduce this test to counting rows. It was exactly that until 2026-07-28: it printed list-length of each requirement list against an .expected naming the counts, and it was the ONLY test guarding 60 regulatory claims. It never read mechanism, class or artifact, so a row naming a mechanism that does not exist kept it green; it derived its number from the list it claimed to verify, so it could only fail when someone edited the list and then updated the .expected; and it pinned NIST at 5 while the 8259A baseline has 6, so correcting the module turned a green test red and the fix read as a regression. A green test called compliance-report beside the compliance module did the rest. Born that shape in CL 4092 (2026-06-13), whose description is "CRA 8 + ETSI 6 + NIST 5 = 19 mapped requirements" -- the count was the deliverable from the start.

author: blu
body: This whitelist is the point of the test, not bookkeeping: it is what makes a typo or an invented artifact name fail rather than pass silently. Fired by sabotage before it was believed -- retyping effect-types as effect-typos moved ETSI to 5 faults, NIST to 1 and IEC62443 to 1 (the seven rows that use it) and left CRA, which uses none, untouched. Truncating one mechanism to "TODO" moved exactly the NIST line and nothing else. If a genuinely new artifact kind is added to ComplianceEvidence, add it here in the same changelist; that is the intended friction.
